request:
Persist GitWeave provenance refs to the remote repository

## Problem

GitWeave currently stores execution provenance locally in Git refs such as:

```text
refs/notes/gitweave/<run-id>
refs/gitweave/<run-id>/run
refs/gitweave/<run-id>/attempts/...
```

However, publishing or merging a Pull Request only pushes the artifact branch/commits. The GitWeave notes and Run refs remain local unless they are pushed separately.

This means execution metadata such as token usage, duration, provider/model information, results, logs, attempts, and Run records can be lost when the local GitWeave checkout is removed. It also prevents later analysis from another machine or from a fresh clone of the repository.

For a Git-native provenance system, the repository's remote should retain the GitWeave execution history needed for later inspection and analysis.

## Expected outcome

Persist GitWeave provenance refs to the remote repository.

At minimum, completed Runs should make the relevant refs available remotely, including:

```text
refs/notes/gitweave/<run-id>
refs/gitweave/<run-id>/run
refs/gitweave/<run-id>/attempts/...
```

and any other GitWeave-owned refs required to reconstruct the Run and inspect Node attempts.

After the local execution environment is gone, a later GitWeave process should be able to fetch the repository and recover the recorded provenance for historical Runs.

The remote provenance should remain available after the associated Pull Request is merged.

This should preserve the distinction between:

```text
normal Git branches / commits
  → repository artifact history

GitWeave-owned refs and notes
  → execution provenance and Run history
```

## Context

GitWeave uses Node output commits as artifact identities and Git notes as execution metadata.

A merge commit can preserve the Node output commits in the target branch ancestry, but the notes themselves are separate refs and are not transferred automatically when a normal branch is pushed.

GitWeave therefore needs an explicit remote persistence mechanism for its provenance refs.

The goal is for the Git remote itself to act as the durable provenance store so that later tooling can analyze historical Runs without depending on the original local checkout.


User directive: GitWeave implements, creates a separate PR, reviews/fixes iteratively and merges only when clean. Stop on unsupported operations or permission/allowance limits and ask the user. No parent manual substitute is authorized. Issue14 is reviewed/published first, then a new GitWeave Run using the reviewed version will merge its existing PR using a merge commit.
